Jasmine / Priyom — quick feasibility check: compressed eval (3 weeks) is technically doable but requires the following trade-offs and actions:

- Trade-offs:
  * Reduced traffic diversity: we scope to two customer-facing flows rather than full corpus.
  * Narrowed metric set: focus on latency, hallucination rate on curated prompts, and throughput under target concurrency.

- Required actions:
  * Temporary increase in support from infra on canary runs (one extra escalation engineer for the first 48 hours of canary).
  * Pre-allocate a 4-GPU burst pool for three weeks (cost uplift estimate attached in eval-plan-v2.pdf).
  * Lock an automated rollback trigger: any >10% regression in hallucination rate or >20% latency percentile degradation triggers immediate rollback.

I'll annotate the MAP and the eval-plan with itemized tasks and rough costs. If procurement will not accept a schedule change, compressed eval with the triggers above is the mitigation.

Rishi
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

1) A clear rollback clause (Rishi's triggers) and a post-eval remediation plan.
2) A fixed uplift fee to cover burst GPU capacity and dedicated escalation support (itemized in eval-plan-v2.pdf).
